s: 'Triclosan', considered harmful when exposed to high levels for a long time, is most likely present in which of the following?
x: Triclosan is a chemical with antibacterial properties. Triclosan is an ingredient added to many consumer products intended to reduce or prevent bacterial contamination. It is added to some antibacterial soaps and body washes, toothpastes, and some cosmetics products. It also can be found in clothing, kitchenware, furniture, and toys. In 2017, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) declared that triclosan is not generally recognized as safe and effective for antiseptic products intended for use in health care settings. In 2016, the FDA also banned over-the-counter consumer antiseptic wash products containing triclosan from being marketed to consumers. These products include liquid, foam and gel hand soaps, bar soaps, and body washes. The basis of the ban was that manufacturers haven't proved that triclosan is safe for daily use over a long period.

Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct
x: Homogeneous solutions have the same composition and properties throughout the solution. None of the components involved in the homogeneous solution can be detected or observed separately. A solution of table salt in a glass of water is an example of a homogeneous solution. A solution having different compositions and properties throughout is a heterogeneous mixture. Individual components of a heterogeneous mixture can be discreetly observed. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

s: Which of the following are the constituents of a soda acid fire extinguisher ?
o: Conc. Sulfuric acid and aluminium sulphate
Dil. Sulfuric acid and sodium carbonate
Dil. Sulfuric acid and sodium bicarbonate solution
Conc. Sulfuric acid and sodium carbonate solution
x: A soda-acid fire extinguisher contains a solution of sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) and Sulfuric acid, which, when mixed, produce carbon dioxide gas that helps extinguish fires by displacing oxygen. Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) is the 'soda' part of the extinguisher, while Sulfuric acid (H2SO4) is the 'acid' part, and it's a diluted solution of Sulfuric acid. When the Sulfuric acid comes into contact with the sodium bicarbonate solution, a chemical reaction occurs, producing carbon dioxide (CO2), water (H2O), and sodium sulphate (Na2SO4). 2NaHCO3 + H2SO4 → Na2SO4 + 2H2O + 2CO2 The carbon dioxide gas produced by the reaction displaces oxygen, which is needed for combustion, thus smothering the fire.

x: An accelerometer is a device that measures the vibration, or acceleration of motion, of a structure. One of the most common uses for MEMS accelerometers is in airbag deployment systems for modern automobiles. In this case, the accelerometers are used to detect the rapid negative acceleration of the vehicle to determine when a collision has occurred and the severity of the collision. A free-fall sensor (FFS) is an accelerometer used to detect if a system has been dropped and is falling. It can then apply safety measures such as turning off and parking the head of a hard drive to prevent a head crash and resulting data loss upon impact. Smartphones, digital audio players and personal digital assistants contain accelerometers for user interface control; often the accelerometer is used to present landscape or portrait views of the device's screen, based on the way the device is being held. Hence, in all three given actions, the function of accelerometer is required. x: Controlled drug delivery in patients is correct: Hydrogels are three-dimensional spatial network systems that use water as the dispersing medium, are soft in nature, can maintain a certain shape, and have strong water absorption capacity (water content can be as high as 99%). In addition, hydrogels have good biocompatibility and biodegradability. They are widely used in biomedical fields. They are extensively utilised in controlled drug delivery systems. They can encapsulate drugs and release them in a controlled manner in response to stimuli such as changes in pH, temperature, or specific enzymes. Mobile air-conditioning system is incorrect: Although hydrogels can absorb moisture and have thermal properties, their application in air-conditioning is not significant. Preparation of industrial lubricants is incorrect: Hydrogels are not used in the preparation of industrial lubricants, which typically require oil-based or synthetic substances for reducing friction.

2. Mobile air-conditioning systems
3. Preparation of industrial lubricants
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Hydrogels are polymeric materials consisting of a sparse network of polymer chains embedded in an aqueous medium. Hydrogels can retain large amounts of water within their intermolecular space due to strong hydrophilicity of the polymer chains and large porosity. Flexibility of hydrogels, which is because of their water content, makes it possible to use them in different conditions ranging from industrial to biological. Hydrogels considerably enhance the therapeutic outcome of drug delivery and have found enormous clinical use. Their porosity and compatibility with aqueous environments make them highly attractive bio-compatible drug delivery vehicles. Owing to their tunable physical properties, controllable degradability and capability to protect labile drugs from degradation, hydrogels serve as a platform on which various physiochemical interactions with the encapsulated drugs occur to control drug release. Hence, point 1 is correct. Hydrogels are flexible and soft 3-dimensional networks with high water content and evaporative and radiative cooling properties that make them suitable for use in passive cooling technology. Hydrogels can be used as desiccants to control humidity. However at present, they are not used in mobile air-conditioning systems. Hence, point 2 is incorrect. Hydrogels can be used in industrial lubricants to improve their properties, such as reducing friction and wear, controlling viscosity, and improving thermal stability. s: The boiling point of water, on the Kelvin scale of temperature, is
x: Water boils at 100°C, which equals 373 K.

s: The hydraulic breaks used in automobiles is a direct application of
x: Hydraulic brakes work by transmitting pressure equally through a fluid, which is Pascal's law, not Bernoulli's theorem or Archimedes' principle.

s: In a Doctor's stethescope, the sound is intensified because of
x: In a stethoscope, sound from the chest is confined in the tube and reflected repeatedly off its walls, so it reaches the ears intensified; this is reflection of sound.

s: The percentage of water in milk is measured by
x: A lactometer measures the specific gravity of milk and so tests its purity, including water adulteration. A hygrometer measures humidity, so it is the tempting wrong option.

s: What is the SI unit of inductance?
x: The SI unit of inductance is the Henry (H); Farad is the unit of capacitance, Ohm of resistance and Candela of luminous intensity.

s: Why a bird standing on a high voltage cable does not get electric shock?
o: The body of a bird is resistant to current flow
Current follows the least path through the electric cable
Feathers of the bird offer protection from electric shock
There is no potential difference between its legs
x: A bird on a live wire touches only one conductor and both its feet are at the same potential, so no current flows through it. Its body resistance or feathers are not the reason.

s: The fourth state of matter refers to:
x: Plasma, an ionised gas of free electrons and ions, is called the fourth state of matter after solid, liquid and gas.

s: Myopia is connected with:
x: Myopia (short-sightedness) is a refractive error of the eye where distant objects appear blurred.

s: Inertia is the property of:
x: Inertia is the property of mass that resists changes in an object's state of motion; greater mass means greater inertia.

s: When there is no external force acts on a system of particles, the velocity of centre of mass of the system will be:
x: According to the law of conservation of momentum, if no external force acts on a system, the velocity of its centre of mass remains constant.

s: If the momentum of a body is increased by 100%, the kinetic energy will be increased by:
x: Since KE = p²/2m, doubling the momentum quadruples the kinetic energy, a 300% increase.

s: The new time-clock invented by American scientists which shows the most exact information is:
x: Atomic clocks, measuring time from atomic vibration frequencies, are the most precise timekeeping devices.

s: If a table-fan rotating at 50 rpm is placed under an electric lamp (AC supply), it would appear to be
o: rotating slowly, both forwards and backwards
x: This is the stroboscopic effect: the flickering AC-powered lamp illuminates the blades at intervals that make the fan appear to rotate slowly backwards.

s: Which of the following is considered by scientists as the 'fourth state of matter'?
x: Plasma, an ionised gas of free electrons and ions, is recognised as the fourth state of matter alongside solid, liquid and gas.

s: An air bubble in water will act like a
x: An air bubble in water has a lower refractive index than the surrounding medium. It diverges light rays and behaves like a concave lens.

s: A myopic eye can be corrected by using a :
x: Myopia or near-sightedness is a refractive error which means that the eye does not bend or refract light properly to a single focus to see the image clearly. In Myopia, close objects look clear but distant objects appear blurred. It is corrected by using a concave lens.

s: The type of mirror used in the headlight of a car is:
x: Car headlights use a concave mirror, which gives a powerful parallel beam when the bulb is at its focus; convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors instead.

s: The formation of glittering colours in thin foam of soap is the result of which of the following phenomenon –
x: The formation of glittering colour in thin foam of soap is the result of the phenomenon of total reflection and interference. When light waves hit a bubble, some of them bounce straight back off the outer part of the soap film. Others refracted on through but then bounce off the inner part of the film. Now interference of refracted and reflected light gives soap foam glittering colour.

s: Decibel is used to measure :
x: 'Decibel' (dB) is used to measure the level of intensity of sound (sound-pressure level) in atmosphere.

s: Which of the following is a cause of echo?
x: An echo is a sound caused by the reflection of sound waves from a surface back to the listener. It is the reflection of sound, arriving at the listener sometime after the direct sound. Echoes are a result of reflections when a sound wave comes into contact with a boundary, particularly a flat and hard surface. Basically a reflection of sound causes echo.

s:
Assertion (A) : The boiling point of water decreases as the altitude increases.
Reason (R) : The atmospheric pressure increases with altitude.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
x: As the density of air becomes heavier near the surface of the Earth (due to gravity) and begins to lighter on higher altitudes, the atmospheric pressure decreases with increase in the altitude. The boiling point of water decreases as the altitude increases. Thus, (A) is true, but (R) is false.

s: Which mirror is used as a rear view mirror in vehicles ?
x: A convex mirror is used as a vehicle rear-view mirror because it gives an erect, diminished image and a wide field of view.

s: A person standing in front of a mirror finds his image larger than himself. This implies that the mirror is :
x: A person standing in front of a mirror finds his image larger than himself implies that the mirror is concave. A spherical mirror, whose reflecting surface is curved inwards, that is, faces towards the centre of the sphere, is called a concave mirror. Concave mirrors are commonly used in torches, search-lights and vehicles' headlights to get powerful parallel beams of light. They are often used as shaving mirrors to see a large image of the face. Dentists use concave mirrors to see large images of the teeth of patients.

s: Relative humidity is measured by :
x: Hygrometer is a device used to determine the relative humidity of the atmosphere. Lactometer is used to measure the density of milk, hydrometer is used for measuring the relative density of liquids while potentiometer is used to measure the electric potential (voltage) in a circuit.

s: Two glass lenses of same focal length, one being convex and the other concave, are kept in contact, the combination will act as :
x: If two glass lenses of same focal length, one being convex and the other concave are kept in contact then resultant focal length of the combination will be infinity and it will act as a plane glass sheet.

s: Which of the following cannot travel in vacuum?
x: Sound waves cannot travel in vacuum. It is transmitted by the movement of particles along with the direction of the motion of the sound wave. More generally, sound is a mechanical disturbance which is dependent upon a medium to travel. It can be transmitted through solid, liquid, and gas.

s: One important characteristic of sound is 'Pitch', which depends upon :
x: The sensation of frequency is commonly referred to as the pitch of the sound. A high pitch sound corresponds to a high-frequency sound wave and a low pitch sound corresponds to a low-frequency sound wave. High pitch means very rapid oscillation and 'low' pitch corresponds to slower oscillation.

s: Which of the following lens is used to minimize Myopia?
x: A concave lens is used to minimize the defect of myopia.

s: Sound waves do not travel in :
x: Sound is a mechanical wave that needs a material medium (solid, liquid or gas) to travel, so it cannot propagate through a vacuum.

s: Which of the following is used by the dentist to see the image of teeth of a patient?
Which instrument is used for measuring humidity in the air?
x: A hygrometer is an instrument used to measure the moisture content in the atmosphere which is also called as humidity in the the air. Spectrometer is an instrument used to measure properties of light over a specific portion of the electromagnetic spectrum. A Eudiometer is a laboratory device that measures the change in volume of a gas mixture following a physical or chemical change.

s: Reading glasses are made from which type of lenses?
x: A convex lens is thicker in the middle and thinner at the edges. Rays of light that pass through the lens are brought closer together. A convex lens is also called a converging lens. A convex lens is used in reading glasses and it also used to remove the defect of far-sightedness.

s: Myopia is corrected by using :
x: Myopia is corrected with a concave lens of negative power, which diverges rays so the image falls on the retina. Convex lenses correct hypermetropia, and mirrors are not used for correction.

s: As the diameter of objective lens of a telescope increases, the resolution of telescope :
o: Depends on focal length of lens
x: Resolution or resolving power is the ability of a telescope to distinguish between two closely spaced objects. The objective lens is the primary lens in a refracting telescope that gathers light from a distant object. A larger objective lens gathers more light, which brightens the image and improves the contrast, making it easier to resolve details. With a larger objectives lens, the telescope can see smaller details and finer features in the image. The resolution of a telescope is limited by diffraction, a phenomenon where light waves bend around obstacles. A larger aperture (diameter) helps reduce the effects of diffraction, leading to sharper images. Thus, as the diameter of the objective lens of a telescope increases, its resolving power also increases, allowing it to distinguish finer details.

s: Because of impurities the boiling point of a liquid –
x: The boiling point of a liquid is the temperature at which its vapour pressure is equal to the pressure of the gas above it. When some impurities are mixed with any liquid, its boiling point increases.

s: In automobile hydraulic brakes work on –
x: Hydraulic brake, hydraulic press, hydraulic elevator all works on the principle of Pascal's law which states that pressure exerted anywhere in a confined incompressible fluid is transmitted equally in all directions throughout the fluid such that the pressure variations remain the same.

s: What type of lens is used in magnifying glass?
x: Convex lenses are used in magnifying devices due to their magnifying properties. A convex lens has the capacity to make an object appear much larger than it actually is. Hence, it is used in the magnifying glass. Magnifying glass is used to enlarge items such as writing so it can be read more easily.

s: Pressure-cooker cooks food in lesser time because
o: The temperature of boiling water decreases due to
Air has no effect as it is closed from all sides
Temperature of boiling water increases due to high
Evaporation of the water used is very small
x: In a pressure cooker the higher pressure raises the boiling point of water (~120 C), so food cooks at a higher temperature and in less time. Option 1 is wrong because the temperature rises, not falls.

s: The density of milk can be obtained by the use of :
x: Lactometer is used for the measurement of the density of milk. Butyrometer is used to measure fat content in milk or milk products.

s: Myopia or short sightedness is corrected by :
x: Myopia or near-sightedness is corrected by using a concave lens. It is a refractive error, which means that the eye does not bend or refract light properly to a single focus to see images clearly. In myopia, close or nearby objects look clear but distant objects appear blurred. A myopic eye forms the image of a far-off object in front of the retina because of the increase in converging power of the eye lens.
